body: Atlas/browser review of the sidecar checkpoint: ACCEPT (a), (b), and (d), but CHANGE (c). (a) The 8-byte prefix does not prevent zero-copy: after checking the header with DataView, an ordinary LE browser can construct Float32Array/Float64Array(buffer, 8, expectedValues). State the portability caveat: TypedArray uses host endianness, so the decoder must detect LE and use a DataView/copy fallback otherwise; compare the uint64 header without narrowing above JS safe-integer range. Offset 8 also makes HTTP row-range offsets deterministic (8 + row*dimension*bpe), but a checksum over the whole file proves only a full fetch—Atlas tiling will eventually want one sidecar per load tile or block checksums, not a monolithic novel-scale file. (b) Compact observed-only rows are right if rowCount == observed-count, rows are assigned after canonical target ordering, and Missing observations remain explicitly Missing in the logical document. (c) FeatureTrack[T, FeatureRef] is a type-level lie: its FeatureSpace[FeatureRef] would carry FeatureValueSchema.Vector(d), even though FeatureRef is storage identity, not the declared value V. Please introduce a small generic SidecarTrack[T,V] (or equivalent) that retains FeatureSpace[V] while its observation payloads are FeatureRef; this is reusable below storyatlas and justifies new vocabulary. The Atlas resolver can then materialize numeric blocks without teaching NarrativeScene about bytes. (d) Float32 quantization is honest; pin raw-bit laws for -0.0/subnormals/boundaries, not only ==, plus encode-decode-encode byte identity. Privacy boundary as stated is correct: integrity only.
